question: X and Y together can complete a work in 10 days. Y and Z together can complete the same work in 12.5 days. Z and X together can complete the same work in 50 days. In how many days can all the three complete the same work while working together?
solution:
**Given:**

X and Y together can complete the work in 10 days

Y and Z together can complete the work in 12.5 days

Z and X together can complete the work in 50 days

**Formula used:**

Work done per day = 1 / Time taken

Let the work done by X, Y, and Z per day be x, y, and z respectively.

**Calculations:**

1) X and Y together can complete the work in 10 days, so: x + y = 1 / 10

2) Y and Z together can complete the work in 12.5 days, so: y + z = 1 / 12.5 = 0.08

3) Z and X together can complete the work in 50 days, so: z + x = 1 / 50 = 0.02

We now have the following system of equations:

1) x + y = 0.1

2) y + z = 0.08

3) z + x = 0.02

Adding all three equations:

(x + y) + (y + z) + (z + x) = 0.1 + 0.08 + 0.02

2x + 2y + 2z = 0.2

⇒ x + y + z = 0.1

The total work done by all three per day is 0.1, so the time taken by all three to complete the work together is:

Time = 1 / (x + y + z) = 1 / 0.1 = 10 days

**∴ All three together can complete the work in 10 days.**
